profile.reading: K-Motion Interactive is a sports-technology company that makes 3D motion-capture and biomechanics analysis systems used in golf and baseball swing instruction, based in the Scottsdale area of Maricopa County, Arizona. The coordinates on file sit within the McDowell Mountain Business Park, a multi-tenant office and light-industrial park, and a check of the address today finds a different small business occupying that specific building. There is no indication that K-Motion, or any current tenant at this location, operates server rooms, colocation space, or dedicated data center infrastructure here. This entry describes the business as it is known publicly rather than presenting an ordinary office address as a data center facility.

reading.body:
K-Motion Interactive is not a data center, and its presence in any Arizona facility count is a mapping error rather than a real asset.

The entry came from an OpenStreetMap point tagged as telecom and data center. The coordinates resolve to a multi-tenant office and light-industrial park in McDowell Mountain Business Park, and the building is now occupied by a different small business. K-Motion itself is a sports biomechanics and motion-capture company selling swing analysis for golf and baseball. It has no server rooms, no colocation space, and no published power figure.

This matters because Arizona's mapped inventory is small and its published capacity is smaller. The state has 56 mapped facilities, of which only 4 publish power figures, totaling 512 MW. A mistagged office adds a row to the first number and nothing to the second. The error inflates the count of sites that might someday draw power, which is exactly the count readers use to judge how much compute the grid is being asked to carry.

The data does not say how many other entries in the Arizona set are mistagged the same way. It does show that the other eight rows in this batch sit 12 to 15 miles away, in Phoenix, Tempe, Mesa, Chandler, and Gilbert, so they are not one shared building either. Each is an independently mistagged small business. That pattern suggests the count is contaminated by a tagging convention rather than by a single bad record, but the data here covers one facility and cannot quantify the rest.
